title: Session references — sign-off gate
lead: Nothing here touches the backend yet — this is all fake data in the design sandbox. Four things below are real decisions only you can make (marked Judgment); the rest are already-built surfaces asking “does this look right?” (marked Measured). Click Yes, No, or Tell me more on each; nothing is built or changed until you say so.

items.title: Search card — open on its own, or stay closed?

points.what: When Claude searches your past conversations, the result card starts closed inside its own closed group — you click twice before you see a Preview button.
points.fix: Leave it closed like every other tool card, or open the results automatically so Preview is one click away.
points.why: This used to open automatically for exactly this reason, and that was deliberately reversed — most searches get skimmed once and scrolled past, so a card that force-opens itself was judged more annoying than useful. Reopening it here trades that back for faster access to Preview/Resume.

items.title: Search results — every state it can show

points.what: One list, eight different situations: found and open, blocked two different ways, gone from this device, a different assistant, no title, unreadable, and simply not found.
points.fix: Confirm this covers everything you'd expect to see — nothing new to design here, just a look before backend work starts.

points.what: When Resume can't work, the row says why in plain words right where the date would be — not hidden behind a hover tooltip.
points.fix: Confirm this reads clearly at a glance.

points.what: A conversation whose transcript is gone from this device disables its Preview button too, not just Resume — there is nothing left to read.
points.fix: Confirm this is the right call rather than hiding the row entirely.

points.what: On a phone, there's no search index yet, so this whole list can't be built — but the small title above it still says “Found 8 past conversations,” a promise the screen underneath doesn't keep.
points.fix: The title needs to stop claiming a list exists when it doesn't — flagged for the phone-specific follow-up work, not a decision for right now.
points.why: Couldn't be screenshotted live — the design sandbox has no way to fake “no phone search index,” so this is confirmed by reading the code that decides what the title says versus what the list falls back to, not by a picture of it actually happening.

points.what: If Claude trims the search command's output itself (piping it through something like “| head -3”), the result renders as plain typed text instead of a card — building a card from a partial answer would risk showing wrong information.
points.fix: Confirm this fallback is the right call.

points.what: When Claude opens one conversation by name instead of searching, the card header says “Past conversation” and shows just that one row.
points.fix: Confirm this wording and layout are fine.

points.what: A technical safety check: the code that recognizes “this line names one conversation” could theoretically be fooled by a search list if two conversation ids were identical for the first 35 characters — vanishingly unlikely, and not something that has ever happened, but worth a one-line fix to close off.
points.fix: Confirm you're fine with a small code fix here, no visual change.

items.title: Reading a past conversation — the top bar

points.what: Left to right: a list toggle, the conversation's title, a Resume button, a tag icon (same one as the resume screen), expand, and close.
points.fix: Confirm this control lineup and order are right.

points.what: Where Claude used tools in between messages (reading files, running commands), the panel marks the gap — here, “3 tool calls not shown” — instead of pretending the conversation flowed seamlessly.
points.fix: Confirm this marker reads clearly.

items.title: Reading a past conversation — scrolling further back
items.surface: Side panel · preview, scrolled to top

points.what: A quiet caption says “Past conversation · read-only · Claude Code”, and a “Load older” button appears once you've scrolled back as far as this panel has loaded — only 40 messages come over at once.
points.fix: Confirm the caption wording and the Load older control are fine as-is.

items.title: Tagging and noting a past conversation

points.what: Clicking the tag icon opens the same tag-and-note editor the Resume screen already uses — nothing new was drawn for this.
points.fix: Confirm reusing that exact editor here is right.

points.what: Right-clicking text inside a previewed conversation offers the same menu the live chat does — Ask about this, Copy, Select all — nothing missing, nothing extra.
points.fix: Confirm this matches your expectations for a read-only view.

items.title: What “Ask about this” types into your message box
items.surface: Composer · after clicking Ask about this

points.what: Picking “Ask about this” on something inside a past conversation types this ahead of your question: “(from the past conversation “Permission ask timeout”, id a3f2aaaa-1111-4111-8111-111111111111) Earlier, you shared this code:”
points.fix: The id has to be in there — it's the only way Claude can go read more of that old conversation — but is the wording OK to send as-is, or does it need to read more naturally?
points.why: Nothing about the exact phrasing has been signed off yet. This is real captured text from the design sandbox, not a mock-up.

items.title: “Referenced conversations” list — keep or cut?
items.surface: Side panel · file list, bottom section

points.what: A running list of every past conversation you've previewed this session sits at the bottom of the file list — shown here with two entries, one from each assistant.
points.fix: Keep it, or cut it? It's the one part of this feature nobody has found a clear need for — the search result cards stay visible in the chat either way, and the reading panel works fine without this list.
points.why: Already built and easy to remove cleanly if you'd rather not have it — this is a genuine “is this worth the screen space” call, not a bug.

items.title: When a past conversation can't be read

points.what: The one you can actually see today: “Couldn't read this transcript: EACCES: permission denied, open '...'” with a Retry button — the real underlying error, not a guess.
points.fix: Confirm this reads clearly to you as a non-developer.

points.what: If a read fails and the app genuinely doesn't know why, it says so instead of guessing: “Unable to read this transcript.” plus “The read didn't report a reason. Diagnosing will collect the app's logs so Claude can look at what happened.” — with Report a bug / Diagnose with Claude buttons instead of Retry.
points.fix: Confirm this wording is honest and clear — this exact screen can't be forced to appear yet, so there's no picture of it, only the wording itself.

points.what: Four more specific reasons a read can fail are written but not wired up to anything yet — read them now so you've seen them before they ever appear: “Not a conversation id” · “This conversation is not in the index on this device” · “This file is a helper transcript, not a conversation” · “Transcript is stored outside the folders YouCoded may read”.
points.fix: Confirm all four read clearly in plain English — no picture for these either, they're not connected to anything yet.

points.what: At phone width the Resume button shrinks to just an arrow icon so the whole row — list, title, Resume, tag, expand, close — still fits without crowding.
points.fix: Confirm this still feels usable at this width.

items.title: The card for a conversation Claude puts in front of you — how do you open it?
items.surface: Design sandbox · locked look, no trigger built

points.what: The look of this card is already locked in (shown here) — but nothing builds it yet, because there's no way for Claude to tell the app “show this conversation”.
points.fix: Three ways to get there: (a) reuse an existing search command as the signal — smallest change; (b) add a new command to the search plugin — but people who already installed it won't get the update until a separate app fix ships; (c) give the YouCoded assistant (not Claude Code) a real dedicated tool for this — a small, contained change, but only works for that one assistant.
points.why: Verified: this app cannot hand Claude Code a brand-new custom tool the way it can for its own built-in assistant — checked by searching for any app-made tool server across the whole codebase; the app only connects Claude Code to other people's tools, or ones reached by typing a command.

closing: That's everything. Four real decisions (D1–D4) plus a look at every other new surface — say the word whenever you're ready for backend work to start.
